newsitem.title: FRANCE: French transport strikes lose grip.
newsitem.headline: French transport strikes lose grip.

text.p: A 12-day drivers' strike disrupting public transport in French cities weakened its grip on Monday after police cleared pickets in Toulouse and employers made concessions to drivers demands' for shorter hours.

In Toulouse, a bastion of the stoppages which began 22 days ago in the south-western city, police cleared about 100 pickets blocking a bus depot shortly after dawn to let about 30 percent of buses run.

Other strikes, which started 12 days ago and have disrupted buses, trams and underground Metro trains in about 20 provincial cities, were still affecting Lille, Nice, Cannes, Clermont-Ferrand, Sete, Toulon and Le Mans.

Unions are divided over whether to recommend a return to work after management late last week met parts of their central demands -- for a cut in the working week to 35 hours with no pay cut and retirement at 55 rather than at 60.

Transport resumed in Perpignan on Saturday. In Lille, strikers were due to ratify a deal later on Monday that would cut the working week to 35 hours from 38 with no loss of salary. It would also grant them an extra two weeks' holiday a year.
In Toulouse, where buses have been running sporadically since a court on Saturday ordered fines for any drivers blocking traffic, non-strikers were operating about 50 buses on Monday.
The strikes are the latest labour challenge to the centre-right government of Prime Minister Alain Juppe, which last year bowed to truckers' demands for retirement at 55 after they blocked roads.
But it has said that state pension funds would be bankrupted if all workers were allowed to retire at 55.
